title: He Will Return in Power
speaker: Jonathan Baird
summary: Jesus chose to walk in weakness though he had unlimited power. He will return as a conquering King, and the whole world will see it.
exhortation: Yesterday Jesus was cleansing the temple, and today we find him with his disciples on the Mount of Olives giving the Olivet Discourse, which I believe is the longest sermon of Jesus in the Gospels.

It's important for Christians to remind ourselves how strong, powerful and in control Jesus is. He came in such humility and weakness that we tend to picture him that way. But though Jesus became weak, even to the point of death, he wasn't actually weak. He chose to walk in weakness while having unlimited power. It's one thing to be humbled when you have no choice. But if at any moment you could turn and destroy your enemies and mockers, could any of us choose to walk in weakness?

That becomes clear in this discourse. Jesus tells his disciples how it will all play out: he will conquer sin and death, and then he will come to judge the world. It won't be meek and mild Jesus anymore. There will be no subtlety. You won't be able to pass him in a crowd without noticing. There will be no doubt who he is and who is in charge.

He tells them this just days before the cross. He knows they will be afraid and full of doubt, and that they are about to watch him suffer and die. So he assures them of the plan: he will conquer, and he will return in power and great glory, not in weakness and with little fanfare like the first time. This time the whole world will be watching in awe. We need that reminder too. We serve a conquering King, the sovereign Lord of lords, who will return in judgment. Every enemy will cower before him, and those he died to save will rejoice and worship with joy and gladness. What a glorious future, and what a glorious Savior.
prayer: Lord, what a hope we have in you, Jesus. There is a day coming when you will return, and every sin and every weight of this world that clouds and distorts our lives today will melt away.
We will see you risen and reigning, clothed in righteousness, ruler of all, the one who spun the stars, the firstborn of all creation and the firstborn from the dead. How we long for that day, Lord.
